data.title: Cartier's latest creations honour the animal world
data.description: Cartier unveils a universe of wildlife that has long been part of the maison's creative world. Since the dawn of the 20th century, birds, insects, reptiles, felines and chimeras have inhabited Cartier's extraordinary fauna, presided over by the panther, the maison's emblematic creature. In its latest creations, alongside the panther, Cartier brings the tiger, parrot, carp, crocodile and rhinoceros to life through jewellery and watchmaking creations. Blending naturalism with imagination, each creation captures the distinctive anatomy and character of these creatures with a remarkable sense of life and movement. Behind every creation lies the savoir-faire of multiple métiers, from sculpting, engraving and polishing to intricate gem-setting. Every detail, from fur and scales to textures and movement, is meticulously interpreted, transforming each creation into a sculptural portrait of the animal world with Cartier's exceptional craftsmanship and unmistakable design language.

data.title: United artists
data.description: Fascinating fauna fronts the Métiers d'Art Tribute to the Animal Kingdom series of six concept watches in a pink or white gold 42mm case. The project reinforces Vacheron Constantin's commitment in encouraging innovation through its "One Of Not Many Crafts Programme".

data.title: US 'must choose' whether to end war: Iran president to Fox News
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - It is for the United States to choose whether to end its war in Iran as Tehran does not wish to continue fighting, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News in an interview aired Thursday.

data.title: Bacteria suspected in deaths of hundreds of baby whales off Argentina
data.description: PUERTO MADRYN (ARGENTINA) - A bacterial infection is suspected of killing hundreds of baby whales in the southern Argentine region of Patagonia, a marine mammal expert told AFP on Thursday.

data.title: Mutating the story
data.description: Anyone who grew up in the 90s -- especially during the era when the first-generation PlayStation console was at the height of its popularity -- almost certainly grew up familiar with the Resident Evil game franchise.

data.title: Thailand settle for second as Japan close out in style
data.description: Thailand finished runners-up in Group A of the men's football competition at the Asian Games after a 3-0 defeat to hosts Japan in their final pool match at Toyota Stadium on Wednesday night, a result that had no bearing on either side's passage to the quarter-finals.

data.title: Nene's rocky road to stardom
data.description: Nine years ago, a little girl in Phuket overslept. That single, ordinary mistake would eventually lead her to the global stage -- and to becoming one of Thailand's most talked-about young musicians.

data.title: Navy to retire 10 ageing ships from Oct 1
data.description: The Royal Thai Navy (RTN) will retire 10 vessels from Oct 1 due to deterioration from prolonged service and high maintenance costs.

data.title: GPS trackers for foreign trucks
data.description: Foreign freight vehicles entering Thailand will be required to install GPS tracking devices from Jan 1, 2027, under a measure aimed at improving road safety and strengthening oversight of cross-border transport.

data.title: Panel sounds alarm on teen pregnancies
data.description: Thailand's low birth rate is drawing attention to its ageing population, but unintended pregnancies -- particularly among adolescents -- remain a concern, prompting calls for better sex education and easier access to contraceptive advice.

data.title: Anutin courts US investment
data.description: Thailand is positioning itself as a gateway to Asean's 700 million people, offering US businesses access to regional markets through trade and investment, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said in New York.

data.title: Israel's Netanyahu denounces enemies, allies in fiery UN speech
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, facing a difficult reelection campaign at home, delivered a fiery UN speech Thursday assailing enemies and allies alike -- and sparking uproar in the chamber.

data.title: Hollywood stars among arrests in NY anti-Netanyahu protest
data.description: NEW YORK - Movie star Susan Sarandon and "Hacks" actress Hannah Einbinder were among people detained by police in New York on Thursday as they moved in to break up a protest against Benjamin Netanyahu.

data.title: French actress Marina Vlady dies at 88
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French actress Marina Vlady, who appeared in more than 80 films and picked up a prize at the Cannes Film Festival in 1963, died on Thursday at the age of 88, her family told AFP.

data.title: Israel policies threaten 'life and existence' of Palestinians, Abbas says
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas said at the UN on Thursday that Israeli policies no longer just jeopardized a two-state solution but were now threatening the "very life and existence" of his people.

data.title: Speed king Puripol smashes into semi-finals
data.description: Thailand's sprint sensation Puripol Boonson roared to within a whisker of history on Thursday, becoming the first Thai ever to break 10 seconds on the Asian Games stage, as sepak takraw booked a shot at double gold in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

data.title: Eviction of pensioner puts Spain housing crisis in spotlight
data.description: MADRID — The eviction of an 87-year-old from her Madrid home has highlighted a political paralysis that has thwarted efforts to resolve Spain's chronic housing crisis, fuelling debate before next year's election.

data.title: UK man died putting women, children first in Mozambique jihadist siege
data.description: WINCHESTER — A British contractor trapped during a 2021 siege by jihadists in Mozambique was "unlawfully killed" after refusing to escape by helicopter, insisting women and children be evacuated first, a coroner ruled Thursday.

data.title: 'Piak Poster', National Artist master of film posters, dies
data.description: Somboonsuk Niyomsiri, the Thai National Artist better known by his professional name, Piak Poster, died peacefully on Sept 24 at the age of 93. He painted more than 1,000 Thai film posters before becoming one of the country’s most celebrated directors.

data.title: Israel's US envoy says son fighting for life
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israel's ambassador to the United States said Thursday that his soldier son was fighting for his life after a Palestinian attacker rammed his car into him at a checkpoint in the occupied West Bank.

data.title: 'I was drowning': Iran Nobel winner exposes pain of separation from children
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Iranian Nobel peace prize winner Narges Mohammadi has said her biggest fear is dying without seeing her two children again after being separated from the twins for over a decade, in her memoir published on Thursday.

data.title: Thai filmmaker Piak Poster dies aged 93 on September 24
data.description: Thai National Artist Piak Poster, who died on September 24, leaves a legacy of film posters, acclaimed movies and cinema preservation.

data.title: Eight killed in wave of Russian strikes on Ukraine
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - A barrage of Russian drone and missile strikes pummelled Ukraine on Thursday, killing six agricultural workers in the east alongside two in the capital, Kyiv, the latest in an intensifying exchange of attacks.

data.title: Daeng Somdet silk shines with Thailand’s first AGT winner Nene Royal
data.description: Nene Royal wore Ban Krua’s handwoven Daeng Somdet silk in the AGT 2026 final, bringing the Bangkok community’s historic weaving heritage to a global stage.

data.title: 'Piak Poster', National Artist master of film posters, dies at 93
data.description: ‘Piak Poster’, the National Artist who painted more than 1,000 Thai film posters before becoming one of the country's most celebrated directors, passed away peacefully of old age on Sept 24. He was 93.

data.title: Tigray rebels in ‘full-blown war’ with Ethiopian forces
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Tigray rebels in Ethiopia told AFP on Thursday they were in a state of “full-blown war” with the federal government, as heavy artillery attacks were reported in neighbouring states.

data.title: Myanmar recalls ambassador to Thailand for questioning
data.description: Myanmar has recalled its ambassador to Thailand for questioning, reportedly in connection with the transport of migrant workers into the country.

data.title: Japanese teen smashes swim world record at Asian Games
data.description: NAGOYA, Japan - Japanese 17-year-old Shin Ohashi smashed a swimming world record at his home Asian Games on Thursday, as several teams rounded on organisers over problems dogging the continent’s biggest sporting spectacular.

Meanwhile, “Disney The Magical Stars 2026 at centralwOrld” brought together brand partners to deliver a world-class experience for audiences in Thailand.

data.title: 12Go Data Shows 49% Rise in Thailand Multimodal Travel Bookings, Revealing the Top 5 Routes
data.description: Thailand's islands are increasingly being reached through multimodal journeys, as travellers combine buses, minivans, ferries and — less often — trains and flights to create multi-stop trips, according to travel booking platform 12Go.

data.title: Ex-minister given death sentence for murder of adopted son
data.description: The Criminal Court has sentenced former cabinet minister Soonthorn Vilawan, 87, to death for the murder of a Prachin Buri councillor who was his adopted son. The sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.

data.title: One Bangkok joins Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026 as principal venue partner
data.description: One Bangkok is participating in Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026 and is set to host a range of activities from 5 to 7 October 2026. Positioning itself as a dynamic “Living Classroom”, One Bangkok aims to bridge sustainability principles with real-world practices, fostering greater awareness and understanding of climate action among the public.

data.title: TCG Launches "Nano Plus" to Support Over 100,000 Micro SMEs
data.description: Dr. Ekniti Nitithanprapas, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, presided over the launch of the Nano Plus Loan Guarantee Programme and delivered a keynote address titled “Financial Opportunities for Small Businesses.” Also attending were Mr. Lawaron Saengsanit, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance; Ms. Jindarat Viriyataweekul, Chairwoman of the Board of Directors of the Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation (TCG); representatives of state financial institutions; executives from Non-Bank institutions providing nano-finance services; and public and private sector partners. The event was held at the Kumpanthong Room, 21st Floor, 150th Anniversary Building, Ministry of Finance, on 22 September 2026.

data.title: Thailand slams ‘chaotic’ Asian Games organisation
